artifacts.notes: Complete De ente et essentia, prologue and six web-numbered chapters. The paragraph order is preserved; source wording is not corrected. Plain prose only, without the modern web reference labels; citations follow the parent witness. Not a critical edition or facsimile.
artifacts.rights_basis: Thomas Aquinas thirteenth-century Latin is public domain in the United States. The extraction retains historical Latin prose only; Corpus Thomisticum navigation, tags, modern electronic reference labels and editorial wrapper are excluded. Recorded printing and editorial revisions do not grant Triptych rights in the historical text.

work.author: Thomas Aquinas
work.description: Aquinas's early treatise on being and essence. The chapter on separate substances (Leonine c. 4; c. 3 in some web divisions) argues that in them essence and being differ, that they lack matter, and that each is its own species. A locus is the Leonine chapter number.
work.title: De ente et essentia
